SK9009 The repository is on an older canonical than the tool carries

The managed block is intact and matches its marker, but it is not the canonical this build of Skala ships. Info by design, and it never fails anything. skala config diff --canonical --options prices the bump option by option; skala config sync --apply takes it.

CategoryTool
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeCompilation
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileno — it reads the whole compilation
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since0.6

Why

A canonical bump is a repository-wide reformatting commit, and eighteen repositories must not have to make it on the day it is published. So being behind is information rather than a gate — even config check --strict does not fail on it — and the two commands exist so that the bump can be priced before it is taken, and its commit recorded in .git-blame-ignore-revs once it is.

When it does not fire

The condition compares hashes and the message compares versions, so a payload regenerated without a version bump produces "on canonical 0.1.0; 0.1.0 is available", which is true and unhelpful. Unmanaged files (SK9014) and drifted ones (SK9008) are never reported as behind.
